coder.description: Use when writing code, implementing features, building functionality, or fixing bugs. Applies story-first and skeleton-first discipline so you build the right thing before building it right. Examples: add a login form, implement the payment flow, build this API endpoint.

debug-mode-agent.description: Use when debugging, investigating failures, troubleshooting errors, or figuring out why something is broken. Uses evidence-first investigation to find root cause before fixing. Examples: this test is failing, why does X crash, the API returns 500.

defensive-programming.description: Use when hardening code for production, adding error handling, implementing observability, designing for failure, or reviewing code for production readiness. Examples: harden this for production, add proper error handling, make this resilient.

planning-mode-agent.description: Use when planning work, breaking down features into tasks, organizing what to do next, or estimating scope. Produces concrete task lists with clear sequence and dependencies. Examples: plan this feature, break this down, what should we build first.

requirements-mode-agent.description: Use when gathering requirements, clarifying scope, or translating user needs into development tasks. Asks the right questions before anything gets built. Examples: what do we need to build, help me understand the requirements, what does the user actually want.

spec-reviewer.description: Review specifications, requirements documents, and tickets for completeness, feasibility, and missing edge cases. Use when auditing a spec before implementation, validating requirements coverage, or checking if a ticket is ready to build. Examples: review this spec for gaps, does this requirements document cover all cases, audit this ticket for completeness.

specer.description: Use this agent when gathering requirements, writing specifications, or clarifying project scope. Examples: <example>Context: Starting a new feature that needs clear requirements. user: 'I need to write specifications for a user authentication system' assistant: 'I'll use the specer agent to help define requirements and specifications using systematic methodology'</example> <example>Context: Unclear specifications need investigation. user: 'The requirements document mentions data processing but doesn't specify the format' assistant: 'Let me use the specer agent to apply SPECIFICATION SPECTACLES and clarify the requirements'</example>

system-design-agent.description: Use when designing system architecture, choosing technical approaches, or turning a vague goal into a concrete implementation plan. Examples: design the database schema, how should we architect this, plan the overall system.

test-quality-review-agent.description: Analyzes test code for quality issues including fake-out tests, error string testing, overly complex mocks, and other test smell patterns that undermine test reliability

tester.description: Use when writing tests, setting up test suites, or validating that code works correctly. Writes tests that prove real behavior, not just coverage metrics. Examples: write tests for this, add a test suite, how do I test this.

user-stories-agent.description: Turns Magic 7 assessment results into evidence-backed user stories with measurable victory conditions that developers can actually build

vibe-slop-detector.description: Use when auditing code for AI-generated antipatterns, over-engineering, unnecessary abstraction, or signs that code was written without understanding. Examples: check this for vibe coding issues, audit for AI slop, is this over-engineered.
